title: Birmingham Pub Quiz

questions.q: What name is given to someone from Birmingham, and to the local accent?
Cadbury built its factory and model village in which Birmingham suburb?
Birmingham is often called the city of a thousand what?
Which band, formed in Birmingham in 1968 with Ozzy Osbourne on vocals, is often credited with inventing heavy metal?
Which BBC drama follows the Shelby family, a gang in Small Heath after the First World War?
Which curry, served in the thin steel bowl it shares its name with, was developed in Birmingham in the 1970s?
Birmingham hosted the Commonwealth Games in which year?
Which Birmingham football club won the European Cup in 1982?
Which author of The Hobbit spent much of his childhood in Birmingham?
Which Birmingham band had a UK number one in 1983 with "Red Red Wine"?

notes: Brummie (from Brummagem); see Brummie dialect (Wikipedia) or the Oxford English Dictionary.
Cadbury moved to Bournville in 1879 and built the model village; see Bournville Village Trust or Cadbury World's history pages.
'City of a thousand trades' is a long-standing nickname; see Birmingham (Wikipedia) or Birmingham Museums Trust.
Formed in Aston, Birmingham, in 1968; see Black Sabbath (Wikipedia) or the band's official site.
Peaky Blinders (BBC, 2013-2022), set in Small Heath, Birmingham, from 1919; see the BBC programme pages.
Balti; the name's origin is disputed, so the question no longer claims it.
Birmingham 2022 Commonwealth Games, 28 July to 8 August 2022; see the Commonwealth Games Federation site.
Aston Villa beat Bayern Munich 1-0 in the 1982 European Cup final in Rotterdam; see UEFA.com or Aston Villa (Wikipedia).
Tolkien grew up in Sarehole and Edgbaston, Birmingham; see the Tolkien Society or Birmingham Museums (Sarehole Mill).
UB40's 'Red Red Wine' reached UK No. 1 in 1983; see the Official Charts Company or UB40 (Wikipedia).
